intro: Every rule here exists because something went wrong once. A rule with a gate is checked on every run and fails the build when it breaks; a rule without one is written down and carried by the tooling, with the numbers beside it.

rules.rule: One contract decides which keyword each URL owns. Nothing else may decide it.
rules.why: Two pages targeting one phrase is the cheapest way to lose both. The contract is the only place ownership is written, and a verifier fails the build if it contradicts itself.
rules.evidence: SEO contract OK — 216 URLs, 163 unique primaries, 0 collisions.

rules.rule: Every page file carries its own keyword lock, generated from the contract.
rules.why: A page and the contract drifting apart is invisible until a rewrite quietly re-targets a page. The lock header makes the intent readable where the copy is edited.
rules.evidence: keyword locks OK — 153 page files + 179 module entries match the contract

rules.rule: A hero sells. Keyword and coverage copy go below the fold — 90 words of hero prose, 140 for an article header.
rules.why: The body-sentence optimizer chose the first prose paragraph, which on most templates is the hero subtitle. /bbq-catering-dubai reached 245 words above the fold.
rules.evidence: hero copy OK — 185 pages, median 36 words of hero prose, none over budget

rules.rule: Subkeywords live in sentences. Never in a title, an H1 or a heading.
rules.why: One FAQ per subkeyword put phrases into h3s and pushed pages to 26 FAQs. The contract's own rule is sentences only; the optimizer enforces it and the map counts violations.
rules.evidence: 3 heading collision(s): another page's primary used in a heading here

rules.rule: A page carries 5–8 FAQs. The optimizer adds none to a page already at the cap.
rules.why: An earlier pass added one FAQ per missing phrase: 24–26 per page, with answers repeated word for word across the site.
rules.evidence: the optimizer adds none above the cap; pages already over it are an owner decision

rules.rule: Never write a phrase from the unplaceable list into copy — meal-kit brands, non-UAE cities, foreign regulators, other people's conferences.
rules.why: The harvested keyword pool carries them, and 'Green chef offers gift cards' reached the working tree before it was caught.
rules.evidence: 81 phrases removed from the contract and blocked in the filler

rules.rule: A primary keyword needs measured UAE demand. Zero-volume phrases are fine as subkeywords, never as a page's target.
rules.why: A page aimed at demand that does not exist has nothing to win, however well it is written.
rules.where: the keyword file's next action · Control's demand debt
rules.evidence: 127 of 163 primaries have no measured UAE volume

rules.rule: A Vercel function in api/ imports packages only. No relative imports, ever.
rules.why: Every file in api/ is compiled as its own function; a relative import is not resolved at runtime. The build passes and the endpoint returns 500. It happened twice in one day: /api/e and /api/seo-login.
rules.evidence: api functions OK — 4 self-contained (ask.ts, e.ts, seo-login.ts, submit-lead.ts)

rules.rule: A retired URL redirects, leaves the sitemap, loses its internal links, and says so in the contract. All four signals or none.
rules.why: A half-retired URL keeps collecting links and splitting authority with its replacement.
rules.evidence: Retirements OK — 71 redirects, all four signals agree.

rules.rule: Title under 65 characters, description in range, one H1, canonical present, primary in the title and the H1.
rules.why: The unglamorous half of on-page SEO, and the half that silently rots during a redesign.

rules.rule: Scores come from the built HTML, never from intent. Rebuild and re-snapshot before judging whether a change landed.
rules.why: A score that moved without a rebuild is measuring the previous build.

rules.rule: Every applied change opens an experiment with a window and a verdict. A drop opens a watch proposal — never an automatic revert.
rules.why: 1,615 edits had been made with no baseline, so none of them could be judged.

rules.rule: Nothing writes to the site without a person. The queue proposes; a human accepts.
rules.why: The optimizer can edit 155 pages in a minute. That is exactly why it does not get to decide.
rules.where: build-proposals.py never calls the optimizer · apply-safe.py is not built

rules.rule: A push to main is a release. Run every gate before pushing, never after.
rules.why: Vercel's Git integration deploys production on every push to main.

rules.rule: Credentials live in ~/.config/claude-seo and Vercel environment variables. Never in the repo.
rules.why: A key in a commit is a key that has to be rotated.
